- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift (increasing by ~0.1–0.3 per day) while true prices often dip or show mean reversion after spikes.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 88+), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward — true prices often drop sharply within 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates volatility in mid-to-late forecast horizon (days 15–30), especially when true prices show sudden drops or recoveries.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; true price movements often contain abrupt reversals or “jumps” not captured by model.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shocks (e.g., EU ETS auction events, regulatory changes) — especially in 2023 Q2.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced when historical mean is high (e.g., >85) — model tends to overpredict even when true prices are near or below historical mean.
- Model exhibits “lagged” behavior — true price drops often precede forecast adjustments, suggesting model reacts too slowly to market shocks.
